perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals
observations: Record backlog, raised guidance and recent missile-production framework remain strong cumulative primary demand signals.
The U.S. State Department approved a possible $24.3B Saudi package including 48 F-35s; this is a demand signal, not a booked Lockheed award, and still faces congressional/process risk.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution
observations: Potential foreign military sales reinforce long-duration demand visibility, but approval must not be treated as revenue: congressional review, contract award, delivery timing, industrial capacity and program economics remain execution gates.

contradictions: Strong demand visibility coexists with material cash-flow timing and program-charge volatility.
unknowns: whether Saudi F-35 approval converts to signed award

lineage.searchStrategy: cumulative primary reuse plus materially different independent government-sale signal; approval explicitly not counted as booked revenue
